comparison: Both address claim C21 about inability to reproduce LTEE dynamics. OpenEval marks this as UNCERTAIN due to lack of explicit comparison with LTEE data, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this finding without challenge, marking it as SUPPORTED.

Perfect overlap on claims C113-C119 regarding DFE dependence on mutation rate and rank behavior. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes complexity of non-monotonicity (C119) could benefit from deeper understanding, while peer reviewers accept the solid data analysis without reservation.

High overlap on future directions (C135-C136, C138-C139). Both mark as SUPPORTED. OpenEval frames these as reasonable but untested speculations, while peer reviewers (particularly Reviewer 3) explicitly affirm the potential for machine learning applications and future work.

Strong overlap on simplified mechanistic model claims (C90-C95). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes qualitative agreement despite quantitative discrepancies due to correlation effects. Peer reviewers emphasize the models are well-supported and reveal mechanistic origins of fitness dynamics.

Both address epistasis slowing fitness trajectories (C24, C58-C62). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mechanistic interpretation relies on spin glass analogy rather than direct demonstration. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly confirms quantitative characterization and mechanistic explanation, with no concerns raised.

Both address model construction and computational methods (C14-C16, C40, C49-C51 for OpenEval; C14-C20, C40, C50-C51 for peer). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes some parameter choices are arbitrary. All three peer reviewers explicitly praise the computational approach as compelling and an important advance.

Overlap on mutation rate effects (C22-C23, C111). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the β threshold is not precisely determined. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this finding as part of solid data analysis without specific concerns.

Overlap on differential effects of mutation rate depending on epistasis (C103-C105). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes novelty and importance of finding that effective models depend on mutation rate. Peer Reviewer 3 directly confirms this as a key finding about clonal interference's landscape-dependent role.

Overlap on implications and framework utility (C121-C122). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval discusses linearity of beneficial mutation rate with fitness and synthesis of results. Peer reviewers emphasize the framework as an important advance and valuable tool for future work.

Overlap on global epistasis emergence (C69-C70). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency with prior work (Reddy and Desai, 2021) and logical connection to rank/increment patterns. Peer reviewers accept this as part of characterizing the model's behavior and mechanistic origins.

Overlap on background/motivation claims (C1-C5 for OpenEval; C1-C13 for peer). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval affirms appropriate citations and correct characterization of SSWM limitations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this framing, with Reviewers 2 and 3 confirming the context about SSWM limitations.

Overlap on fitness landscape model background (C6-C11). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval confirms accurate summarization of prior work with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this background, with discussion of theoretical simplifications validating the motivation.

Overlap on gap identification (C12-C13). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval confirms accurate characterization of prior work limitations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this motivation through their discussion of SSWM limitations in previous theoretical efforts.

Overlap on computational contributions (C17-C20). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes plausible speedup claims though specific benchmarks not provided, and emphasizes code availability. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the high performance algorithm as compelling and foundational for future work.

Minimal overlap on linearity observation (C123). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this is supported by Figure 3 as part of synthesis. Peer reviewers accept this within broader characterization of fitness dynamics and mechanistic understanding.
